Subject: RFI: Chain-of-custody & export requirements for audit logs

Thanks for taking our RFI. We need a clear description of how Redwood produces and exports audit logs for regulatory review. High-level items we want addressed:
- What metadata is captured per event (timestamps, request IDs, model version, region, caller service, IP)

- Legal hold & preservation workflow (how to freeze/delete flags)
- Export formats, manifest files, and delivery methods (S3, signed links, FedRAMP-compatible transfer)
- Retention windows and the ability to do ad-hoc snapshots for e-discovery

We will share a template RFI spreadsheet (attached) with a few tick-box rows and some custom asks. Please respond with specifics and any evidence artifacts you can provide.

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. I reviewed the template and attached a short diagram that maps Redwood's evidence workflow. Below are concise answers and pointers to artifacts we can provide. I kept it scoped to the audit/export path to align with your reviewers.

1) Captured metadata per audit record:
   - event_ts (UTC ISO8601), request_id (UUIDv4), tenant_id, route/model_id/version, input_hash (SHA256 over request payload), response_hash, latency_ms, node_id, region, identity (API key/service account), and optional client_ip

2) Tamper-evidence & immutability:
   - All audit records are written to an append-only internal ledger. Each export includes a signed manifest (SHA256 of concatenated export file checksums) signed with a KMS-backed key. For Private customers we support HSM-backed signing.

3) Legal hold / preservation:
   - Per-tenant legal_hold flag prevents scheduled deletion and promotes data to cold archival with a retention override. We provide a playbook for legal holds (export + notarized manifest).

4) Export formats & delivery:
   - Primary exports: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with one audit event per line, plus a JSON manifest. Secondary: parquet (for analytics). Delivery: direct S3 path (pre-signed URL or cross-account replication), secure TLS transfer, or Kafka topic subscription for streaming tails.

5) Retention & ad-hoc snapshots:
   - Default retention: 90 days hot, 365 days with standard archival. Dedicated/Private options can extend to multi-year (configurable up to 7 years). Ad-hoc snapshot API supports point-in-time export with manifest and hash verification.

Attachments: chain_of_custody_flow.png, export_schema_ndjson_v2.json

I'll follow up with a short export sample and example manifest. If you want a deep technical doc (signed manifests, key rotation frequency, or sample NDJSON with checksums) we can produce that within 48 hours.

-naomi
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Chain-of-custody & export requirements for audit logs

Tom —

Good questions — answers below with specifics we can include in the sample export.

• Manifest & per-file checksums: yes. Each exported data file includes an internal file-level SHA256 and a record_count. The export package contains a manifest.json that lists { filename, size_bytes, sha256, record_count, created_ts }. The manifest itself is signed with an asymmetrically-signed envelope using a KMS key (RSA-4096 or ECDSA-P256 depending on environment). For Private deployments we can optionally provide HSM (PKCS#11) signatures.

• Monotonic sequence numbers: every audit event contains a sequence_id (64-bit monotonic sequence per-tenant+shard). Sequence gaps are detectable and we surface a gap report in the manifest metadata.

• Legal hold audit trail: actions are recorded as separate audit events (actor, actor_email, action=legal_hold_set/cleared, reason, timestamp). We can export the legal_hold_history.csv/ndjson alongside the event export. That file is included in the signed manifest.

• Key rotation & verification window:
   - Rotation cadence: default 90 days (configurable).
   - When a signing key is rotated we keep the previous public keys in the keyset and sign a keyset manifest so verifiers can validate signature chains. There is a 7-day dual-signing window to facilitate verification during rotation; we record which key(s) signed each manifest.

• Sample delivery & verification helpers: we'll provide a 100-event NDJSON sample, the manifest.json, and a short verification script (Python) that computes file SHA256 and verifies the manifest signature using the included public keys.

Next steps: I'll attach the sample export by tomorrow. Can you confirm the preferred delivery method (S3 cross-account, pre-signed URL, or secure SCP)? Also looping Kirk from Auditify in case you want an independently verifiable attestation.

-naomi
